text: The projector in seminar room 4 has been flickering for three weeks now. Our group presented our capstone proposal yesterday and the screen kept going blank every thirty seconds, so the panel missed half of our architecture diagram. We reported it to the help desk twice and both times were told it was 'logged'. Nothing has changed and two other groups present in that room next week.

I really want to thank the tutor for the extra revision session on recursion. She went through every past-year question step by step, drew the call stack on the whiteboard and let us ask as many questions as we needed. It was the first time the topic actually made sense to me. If this could become a regular thing before each quiz it would help a lot of people who are too shy to ask in class.

The group project rubric gives 30% for 'innovation' but nobody can tell us what counts as innovative. Two tutors gave completely different answers in the same week, one said using a new library is enough and the other said it has to be a feature no other group has. We are now three weeks from submission and still guessing, which is stressful when it is such a big part of the grade.

This week I had a lab report, a reflection journal, a quiz and a group milestone all due between Tuesday and Thursday. None of them are hard on their own but together I slept maybe five hours a night. It feels like each module plans its deadlines without looking at the others. A shared calendar across modules would make such a difference.

I am writing this because I don't know who else to tell. One of my groupmates has been sending messages late at night saying they can't see the point of continuing and that everyone would be better off without them. They stopped replying today and did not come to class. I am really worried and I don't know if I should contact someone at the school or their family.

The canteen has cut the vegetarian options down to one stall and it sells out by 12:15 most days. Those of us with labs until 12:30 end up with nothing but chips or vending machine snacks. The prices also went up again this month. I've started skipping lunch on lab days, which is not great when the afternoon session runs until six.

I applied for a leave of absence for a family emergency two weeks ago and submitted the form and the supporting documents on the portal. The status still says 'received'. Meanwhile I have missed a quiz and I have no idea whether it will be excused. I called the office and was told to wait for an email. Some kind of expected timeline would really help.

Shout-out to the student committee for the cultural night last Friday. The food was great, the performances were fun and I finally talked to people from the other cohort that I only ever see in the corridors. I think events like this make the campus feel a lot less like a place you just come to for classes.

The new study pods in the library are nice and quiet, but the booking system only lets you reserve one day in advance and they are all gone by 8am. It would be fairer if each person could only book two hours a day so more students get a chance. Otherwise the pods themselves are a great addition.

The recorded lectures for the networking module still use slides from 2022 with commands that no longer work on the lab machines. We spend the first half of every lab working out what the new command is. The content itself is good and the lecturer explains well, but someone needs to update the examples.

Placement applications close in two weeks but the list of partner companies was only released yesterday, and half the links on the portal are broken. Several of us also haven't received the CV review appointment we booked a month ago. This is the most important thing for our final year and it feels very disorganised.

Not really feedback about a module, just wanted to say the lost and found counter returned my laptop charger within a day which was really nice. Also the vending machine on level 2 keeps eating coins. Thanks.
The air conditioning in the computing lab is broken again and it is too hot to concentrate during the three-hour practical.
The new attendance app logs us out every time we switch apps, so half the class gets marked absent.
